prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1384; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the insured's policyholder reporting a sideswipe while changing lanes on a multi-lane road. The claimant reports neck and back strain and is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver is named on it and that coverage was in force at the time of the loss. Nothing in the file suggests any damage occurred before the coverage start.

Entry 3: Photos taken at the scene confirm the general position of both vehicles and the contact area on the body panels. There are no independent witnesses to the lane change, so the account rests on the parties and the photos.

Entry 4: Spoke with the claimant, who gave the same account of the lane change and impact as in the initial report. Asked about seating position in the vehicle at impact; the answer was not fully clear and will need follow-up.

Entry 5: Reviewed the medical records. The reported neck and back strain fits well with the type and force of the collision. The records also note a minor strain in the same area several years ago that healed fully, which has been added to the file for context.

Entry 6: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this kind of injury. The treating provider's notes are being requested to understand the course of care. It is not yet clear how much of the total damage came from this impact alone.

Entry 7: No prior damage to the vehicle is known from the file or the repair history. Next steps are to obtain the full treatment notes, request the seating information again, and complete the damage review before setting a settlement position.
